title: Minimum Absolute Difference Between Elements With Constraint
statement: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `x`. Consider every pair of indices `i` and `j` whose distance `abs(i - j)` is at least `x` (when `x` is 0, `i` and `j` may be the same index). Return the smallest value of `abs(nums[i] - nums[j])` over all such pairs.
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every pair is O(n²). It is enough to look at each pair once, with `j` as the later index: then `i` may be any index from `0` to `j - x`. As `j` moves right, that allowed range grows by exactly one element, `nums[j - x]`. Keep those allowed values in a sorted container; the value closest to `nums[j]` is either the smallest one at least `nums[j]` or the largest one below it, and binary search finds both.

## Approach

1. Keep `sorted`, the allowed earlier values in increasing order, and `best`, the smallest difference so far.
2. For each `j` from `x` to the end, insert `earlier = nums[j - x]` at its sorted position.
3. Find `pos`, the first position whose value is at least `nums[j]`.
4. Compare `nums[j]` with `sorted[pos]` (its ceiling) and `sorted[pos - 1]` (its floor) when they exist, and keep the smaller gap in `best`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4, 3, 2, 4]`, `x = 2`. For `j = 2`, insert `nums[0] = 4`: `sorted = [4]`; `nums[2] = 2` gives `pos = 0` and gap `4 - 2 = 2`, so `best = 2`. For `j = 3`, insert `nums[1] = 3`: `sorted = [3, 4]`; `nums[3] = 4` gives `pos = 1`, ceiling gap `4 - 4 = 0` and floor gap `4 - 3 = 1`, so `best = 0`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) comparisons for the binary searches; each `splice` also shifts up to n elements, which is a fast memory move in practice. A balanced tree such as Java's `TreeSet` makes every step O(log n).
- Space: O(n) for `sorted`.

## Pitfalls

- Insert `nums[j - x]` before querying `nums[j]`, so that pairs exactly `x` apart count; with `x = 0` this pairs an element with itself and correctly gives 0.
- Check both neighbours of the insertion point: the closest value can be just above or just below `nums[j]`.
- Only the later index needs a loop; pairs with `i > j` are the same pairs seen from the other side.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sorted` | values `nums[0..j - x]` in increasing order |
| `best` | smallest difference found so far |
| `j` | the later index of the pair |
| `earlier` | `nums[j - x]`, the value that just became allowed |
| `pos` | first index in `sorted` with a value at least `nums[j]` |
